Alice Glass (formerly of Crystal Castles) shares first solo single "Stillbirth" along with a letter about an abusive relationship and a donation link to RAINN.
The single will be available on iTunes and Spotify starting July 18th. All proceeds from digital sales will go to RAINN and similar organizations.  https://soundcloud.com/aliceglasss/stillbirth   The letter:   >Years ago I began the process of trying to remove myself from an abusive relationship that started when I was a teenager. Over the course of that relationship I was systematically cut off from anyone and everyone that I could truly be close to. I was talked down to, yelled at, locked into rooms and criticized daily about my abilities, my weight, my looks, my intelligence and almost every move I made. When I couldn't take it anymore and I wanted to end the relationship I was threatened, then I was told I was loved, and the cycle would begin again.   >I want young women and young men to understand that this kind of treatment of others can happen where it might be least expected. Even in environments that thrive on creativity and open-mindedness, that advocate artistic and counter-culture ideals. Sometimes people will use these things to camouflage themselves so that their abuse might go unnoticed. So that you wouldn't think to consider it could be happening right in front of you.  >The clarity I've gained since getting out of that situation has opened up my life in a way that I didn't imagine was possible. Although some of the pain and anger still lingers, my life finally feels as though it has value and meaning. I speak out now hoping that I can encourage other young women and young men to affirm their value within their relationships or get out. Abuse isn't always obvious and it doesn't have to involve black eyes, blood and broken bones. Emotional and psychological abuse can be just as damaging, and it is extremely difficult to remove yourself from.   >Those that have known me throughout my career might be surprised that someone who publicly gave the impression of being fearless and seemed as though they didn't take shit from anyone could find themselves being severely mistreated and manipulated by someone they were close to. This person nearly stripped me of myself. And for years I felt as though they were waiting for my life to end.  >Stillbirth was written by myself and Jupiter Keyes in our basement. There is no label involved. It will be available through iTunes, Spotify, etc. beginning July 18. All proceeds for digital purchases of this song will benefit organizations (like the nonprofit RAINN) that help survivors of domestic abuse, sexual violence and incest. You can donate directly to them at https://donate.rainn.org/ or via the link on my website at http://www.alice-glass.com/   >There is a sister song to Stillbirth that I hope to release soon, she is a lullaby and she can't wait to meet you

I spoke barely more than a sentence out loud today. Things feel more and more "over" every day.
The worst thing about being alone for me is that I know objectively that it's easy to connect with people and maintain a rewarding life. But not doing any of that will always be easier so I can't make myself just change. I wake up every day feeling just exhausted enough that I can't make anything productive out of the day. I know it's supposed to be one day at a time, but all I do is walk just up to the precipice of meaningful change and turn around because I'd rather fall back into familiar comforts. I'm afraid that an active life will stress me out to the point of desiring suicide, so instead I've committed myself to running out the clock until I'm dead. I'm sick of people who only like me for who they think I am. I've never felt loved for who I really am, by family or anyone. On paper, I had a "good" childhood. But my dad is so relentlessly optimistic that it only feels hollow. Why does he say I'm good? Even he must see that isn't true. Every time he acts supportive I know he's masking disappointment. He just wants me to be better in whatever way doesn't neccessitate his direct involvement. I don't have the heart to tell him it's not possible.

Posting this while in a good mood, in hopes that I can sustain it.
I hope this isn't rule-breaking, I won't be offended or hurt if it needs to be removed. I'm not posting this seeking participation from anyone else, it's strictly for my own benefit because it feels helpful for me to unload these thoughts in a public space. I may or may not delete it myself depending on how I feel in the future. I just feel like posting it at the moment.   Whenever I manage to break from depression, I tend to let myself fall back into old habits almost immediately and my progress is lost. I wanted to take a moment to write up a post I can look back on whenever I forget what got me here. Mostly it's not talking things out, because when I keep all my problems to myself they become overwhelming and I tend to make them seem bigger than they really are. I've noticed every time I've broken from my depression it's been through taking 3 easy steps: 1. Saying what's been on my mind in some sort of way where I know someone else could acknowledge it. 2. Changing my perspective. 3. Not allowing myself to become passive or inactive (this means making my own comfort a priority, and not putting things off unless I actually need to.).   One of the main reasons I let myself fall into my old habits is that I end up convincing myself that no matter what, feeling better is only temporary. Of course, it seems clear to me right now that the best thing I can do is find something productive to do each day to make myself feel better. Binge watching TV, eating junk and sitting on the computer can satiate me temporarily, but that usually leads me back into depression and it becomes a cycle. Maybe the best thing I can do is find something new each day or week, until the majority of my bad habits are replaced by new, better habits. Or maybe I don't have to do that. I don't need to have everything figured out at once. It's just nice to shake things up. That's one of my main problems, always thinking in terms of the future and not living in the moment. It leads to me believing I need to understand everything in absolutes, which encourages me to develop a routine, which causes me to stagnate and fall into depression again. Maybe that's because I just shut down and let myself get absorbed in doing next to nothing for way too long. Accepting things the way they are day in, day out is just not healthy for me. I need to take risks.
